title: Video Production in Paris: Films, Motion, 2D and 3D | 22 Signals
description: Video production and animation for Paris brands: launch films, fashion week content, motion graphics, 2D and 3D explainers and AI video, with French versions.
h1: Video production in Paris for launches, collections and complex ideas
intro: We make video and animation for Paris companies: launch films, fashion week and event content, motion graphics, 2D and 3D explainers and AI video. Each project starts from where the film will be watched and what it must do, and French subtitles, voiceover or versions are arranged with partners when your audience needs them.

sections.h: Three kinds of Paris video brief
p: Most of the video work Paris companies need falls into three groups. The first is brand and product films for luxury, fashion and beauty, where every frame is judged against the house's visual standard. The second is fast content: fashion week coverage, event highlights and social cuts that must be online within hours. The third is explanation: a fintech product, a B2B service at La Défense or a deep-tech startup from Station F that needs a complicated idea made clear in ninety seconds.

These need different skills, and many studios are good at only one. Our team covers live action coordination, editing, motion graphics, 2D and 3D animation and AI video, so one plan can cover a launch film, its social cuts and the explainer that sits on the product page.

list: Launch and brand films for collections, products and openings.
Event and fashion week content: highlights, interviews and same-day social edits.
Motion graphics for campaigns, presentations and social media.
2D animated explainers for products, services and processes.
3D animation for products, packaging, buildings and mechanisms that are hard to film.
AI video for concept work, variations and formats where it suits the brand.
Managed editing: ongoing cutting of your own footage into formats for each platform.

sections.h: Fashion weeks, launches and fast turnarounds
p: Paris fashion weeks put more brands, press and buyers in one city than almost any other event. Content from a show or a presentation is most valuable in the first hours, so the edit plan, music rights, captions and formats are settled before the day, not after it. The same goes for product launches, store openings and trade fairs across the city.
We plan these as live operations. Shot lists, file transfer, editing slots and approval steps are agreed in advance, so the first cut reaches you while the event is still being talked about.

Paris has a deep bench of technical companies: AI startups, fintech, health tech, energy and industrial firms. Their products are often hard to film because the value sits in software, in data or inside a machine. Animation solves that. A 2D explainer can show how a platform moves money; a 3D sequence can show the inside of a device without a single prototype.

We start these projects with the script, because the script is where clarity is won or lost. We write it with your product team, test it on someone outside the company and only then move to design and animation.

Many Paris films need to work in French and in English, and sometimes in more languages for European or Asian markets. Our own delivery is in English. French subtitles, voiceover and on-screen text are arranged with native-speaking partners, and you approve them before release.

We plan for this early. On-screen text is kept in editable layers, timings leave room for longer French lines and voiceover is recorded to picture, so each language version looks like it was made for that audience rather than patched afterwards.

sections.h: Rights, releases and filming in Paris
p: France takes image rights seriously. People who appear recognisably on camera generally need to agree to how their image is used, so we collect written releases from cast, models and interviewees, and plan crowd shots with that in mind. Music, fonts and stock footage are licensed for the uses and countries you need.

Filming in public spaces in Paris usually requires permission from the city, and popular locations book up around major events. We factor permits and timing into the schedule. For AI video, we are clear about which models we use, what source material went in and how the output may be used, so your legal team is not surprised later.

A single launch in Paris can need a dozen deliverables: a widescreen hero film for the website and in-store screens, vertical cuts for Instagram and TikTok, square versions for feeds, short loops for product pages and a silent captioned version for LinkedIn. Each has its own length, safe areas and text rules.

We plan the master edit so these versions come out cleanly, rather than cropping a widescreen film at the last minute and losing the product from the frame. Files are named, organised and delivered so your team can find the right one without asking.

list: Talk: a 15-minute call about the audience, the platform and the deadline.
Plan: concept, script, style frames and a production schedule in a written roadmap within 5 to 7 days.
Build: production, animation and editing, with review rounds and delivery dates agreed in writing.
Grow: cut-downs for each platform, performance review and new versions where the numbers say so.

sections.h: Video that works with the rest of your marketing
p: A film is only as useful as the places it appears. Because the same team runs websites, search and paid media, we plan video with its distribution in mind: the six-second cut for paid social, the vertical version for stories, the captioned version for silent autoplay and the full film on a page built to rank. That avoids the common Paris problem of a beautiful launch film that only lives on the brand's own channels.

sections.h: Proof, and working with us from Paris
p: We have broadcast more than 20 live events, which is why we treat deadlines on event and launch content as fixed. We will show you relevant work on a call; client names stay private.

We have no office in Paris. Pre-production runs remotely on shared hours, with Paris one hour ahead of London, and we travel for shoots, events and key reviews when the project needs it, planned into the scope from the start.

faqs.a: Yes, when a project needs it. We plan travel, crew and permits into the scope. Many projects, such as animation, motion graphics and editing your existing footage, need no shoot at all and run fully remotely.

faqs.q: How fast can you turn around fashion week or event content?
faqs.a: With planning done beforehand, first social edits can be delivered on the day. We agree shot lists, formats, music and approvals in advance so editing starts as soon as footage arrives.
Yes. Our delivery is in English, and French subtitles, voiceover and on-screen text are arranged with native-speaking partners. You approve every language version before release.

faqs.q: When does animation make more sense than filming?
faqs.a: When the product is software, a process or something inside a device, or when the item does not exist yet. Animation also makes language versions and later updates easier than reshooting.

faqs.q: Is AI video right for a luxury brand?
faqs.a: Sometimes, for concept work, mood films or many variations of one idea. For hero brand films most houses still prefer filmed or fully crafted animation. We advise case by case and are open about which tools we use.

faqs.q: What does video production in Paris cost with you?
faqs.a: It depends on length, style, whether filming is needed, the number of versions and languages and the turnaround. We price from the brief and give a written scope with delivery dates.
